account: Researchers at Uppsala University and the Karolinska Institutet in Sweden ran parallel virtual screens of large chemical libraries against AlphaFold models and traditional homology models of the trace amine-associated receptor 1 (TAAR1), a target for neuropsychiatric drugs without an experimental structure at the time. They tested 30 top-ranked compounds from the AlphaFold screen and 32 from the homology screen. Eighteen AlphaFold compounds were TAAR1 agonists, a hit rate of 60%, against seven homology compounds (22%), and the three most potent agonists came from the AlphaFold screen. One agonist with a good selectivity profile changed body temperature and showed antipsychotic-like effects in wild-type mice, with no such effect in TAAR1 knockout mice. Science Advances published the study on 7 August 2024. The authors tested the lead only in mice, and they state that AlphaFold was designed to predict a single static structure. Five authors are inventors on a patent application that covers compounds from the study.

ai_role.statement: The researchers ran the same screen against AlphaFold models and homology models and tested compounds from both, so they isolate the contribution of the AlphaFold structure.
